change.scope: exactly one register level on htab_p3v_q[12:0] -> htab_q[49:37] -> bm_raddr_b -> bm_b.addrb
change.mechanism: new flop bm_b_spec_q[12:0] captures the htab read data (hent[49:37], or htab_byp_data[49:37] for the write-first bypass) on every s1_en cycle; the bm_b port address for the scan-phase speculative read is that flop (s1_en ? bm_b_spec_q : S_EXT ? ext_faddr : raddr). No htab ERAM clk2q output drives a bm_b ERAM address any more.
change.option_used: variant of approved option 3 (bm_b read data registered, hit consume delayed one beat) because option 1/2 were infeasible inside the single allowed cone: issuing the htab address one cycle earlier needs the position pos+3 hash bytes, whose third byte is bm_a_rd (an ERAM clk2q output, the path r0 bm-prefetch had just removed), and registering htab_p3v_q without shifting the consumer keeps the same-cycle dependence.
change.consume_realignment: hit cycle H registers cq_r = bm[pos+3]; S_EXT gets one wait cycle that (a) registers the k=0 compare (cq_r vs bm[ref+3]) and (b) advances ext_raddr/ext_faddr to pos+4/ref+4, so from the first decision cycle on the compare/advance stream is byte-for-byte the old one; only the decision (and therefore len_r) is one cycle later. ext_zero_r/len_cap_r keep the values loaded by the hit during the wait cycle.
untouched: htab_p3v write encoding {valid, pos+3[12:0]}, htab/bm sizes, enc_bank layout, htab_b/tag/pos fields
